newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish mixed, near day's highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish mixed, near day's highs.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended narrowly mixed in quiet afternoon trade, with most contracts near the day's peaks.

September Treasury bond futures suffered from technical weakness early Friday and slipped through support to hit a 112-27/32 session low. But in the last hour of trade, most contracts climbed to new session highs as U.S. stocks failed.
Talk circulated of asset allocation out of stocks into bonds, but many debt futures traders discounted that theory.
"Everybody is talking about it but nobody saw it," a T-bond futures trader said.
"It sure traded like it, though," he added.
He called market performance Friday favorable, and said September T-bonds should start next week on a sound footing.
"The market did okay on the week," the trader said. "In my view it was a very good close structurally for the day."
Other traders called overall market volume light, and said action was consolidative after a choppy week.

"It was a real moderate move down in terms of volume and a real moderate move back up," agreed Kurt Fraim, futures analyst with Aubrey G. Lanston. He noted there were no violent price swings on the day, as seen earlier in the week.
"It was in like a lion and out like a lamb for this week," another T-bond futures trader said.

Eurodollar futures briefly were assigned fast market status in the last hour, but overall action there was light as well. Traders said the focus had switched to pre-weekend positioning and next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"They're going to short-cover into the meeting," said Jim Hyerczyk, JAH Research and Trading technician. "There's room to retrace up to 114-15/32," he said.
Traders said market sentiment was for no change in U.S. monetary policy at Tuesday's FOMC, but last-minute jitters could infect the market.
"After a rough and tumble week, we took it easy today," another trader said. "We're waiting on next week and the FOMC meeting, but there really shouldn't be any surprises there."

At the close, September T-bonds were unchanged at 113-20/32, 10-year notes rose 2/32 to 109-13/32, muni bonds fell 2/32 to 119-23/32, December Eurodollars rose 0.045 to 94.140, and T-bills added 0.045 to 94.840. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:chicago.derivatives.newsroom@reuters.com
